text:
Alex: Heads-up — after the KV cache refactor I want a controlled replay canary against production traces to validate determinism and perf parity. Who can own a short run?
Rachel: I can prep the anonymization pipeline and sampling config. we should avoid full-trace replays (costy) so a stratified sample + suffix-preserving anon.
Sam: FYI sampling needs to preserve seq length distribution. If we just uniform-sample we blow up tail latency differences. suggest stratify by model + seq_len_bucket.
Rachel: Agreed. Plan: 1) anonymize user IDs + prompt text, 2) sample traces by (model,seq_bucket,client_tier), 3) enforce deterministic ordering and fixed RNG seed.
PerfBot: replay-harness v2.4 queued: trace_batch=prod-2026-03-10 sample_rate=0.03 anonymize=true seed=20260310
Maria: Note on determinism: CUDA kernel choice can be non-deterministic across runs if we let the runtime pick heuristics. Need to force kernel policy or log kernel IDs. Also watch fp16 vs q4 conversions.
DevOps: Trace access and retention: I can stage a trimmed S3 bundle with ACLs. Will share presigned link once anonymized. Size target ~ 2GB.
Alex: @Rachel can you add parity checks so we compare token-level outputs (hashes) and latency/tokens-per-second? Also capture KV cache hit stats.
Rachel: Yes. I'll produce a small checklist and a run command. parity checks = exact-hash then tolerant-diff for sampling-induced ordering changes.
Sam: For parity we should run two modes: (A) bitwise/seeded deterministic run with kernel_policy=force and (B) default-policy run to see divergence surface. That gives us apples-to-apples + real-world variation.
Rachel: Here's the run command I'll use for the deterministic canary:
```
python tools/replay_run.py \
  --trace s3://redwood-prod/traces/anon/2026-03-10-bundle.tar.gz \
  --anonymize true \
  --sample-config configs/sampling/stratified-0.03.json \
  --seed 42 \
  --kernel-policy force_cpu_gpu_match \
  --output ./replay_results/deterministic_run_20260310 \n```
Rachel: And the default (apples-to-apples) baseline: change kernel-policy to auto and seed to 0.
PerfBot: preliminary: replay harness will emit: per-request {latency_ms, tokens, kv_cache_hits, kernel_id, model_variant}. Aggregates every 10k requests.
Maria: Add a profiler capture (nvprof/tao) on a single host for a subset of heavy traces to correlate kernel_id -> time. Also collect GPU clocks + mem stats.
Alex: Good. Also add a lightweight checksum: md5 of response tokens + model_version string. Store both to detect drift without needing raw outputs.
Sam: On sampling bias: when you stratify by client_tier, include some cold-start sessions; production traffic is 12% cold sessions and they stress KV warmup.
Rachel: Noted. I'll tweak sampling config to ensure cold-session fraction matches production.
DevOps: Uploaded anonymized bundle to presigned link: https://s3.redwood.example/anon/2026-03-10-bundle.tar.gz?sig=REDACTED (expires in 24h)
Alex: Thanks. Target: run deterministic canary on staging cluster first, then a small run on dedicated infra that mirrors prod GPU types. If parity passes, schedule a broader run overnight.
Maria: If we see kernel_id mismatch but perf parity, that's OK. We only fail parity if token outputs differ or tail P99 latency regresses >10%.
Sam: Also log request ordering and replay timestamps; sampling can shuffle, and we need to attribute KV cache misses to replay order vs original runtime behavior.
Rachel: I'll commit the sampling config + parity script to repo: infra/replay/configs/stratified-0.03.json and infra/replay/tools/parity_check.py. Quick snippet of parity CLI: 
```
# parity_check.py usage
python parity_check.py --baseline ./replay_results/default_run --candidate ./replay_results/deterministic_run --report ./replay_results/parity_report.json
```
Alex: Can someone own the run and post results here? quick checklist: 1) anonymized bundle staged (DevOps) 2) sampling config checked in (Rachel) 3) deterministic + default runs completed (owner) 4) parity + perf report (owner) 5) kernel/profiler artifacts uploaded (Maria)
Sam: I'll volunteer to own the runs this afternoon. I'll run deterministic on staging, then default on a matching dedicated node.
PerfBot: run-started: id=rr-20260310-177150 run_owner=Sam mode=deterministic nodes=1 sample_rate=0.03
Sam: Starting now. I'll stream logs to /var/logs/replay/rr-20260310-177150.log and post summary when done.
Alex: Awesome — ping me with the parity_report and the profiler tarball. If we hit regressions we'll open a debug ticket and attach kernel_id timelines. :eyes:
PerfBot: run-complete: id=rr-20260310-177150 status=complete requests=64,321 p50=42ms p95=210ms p99=870ms tokens/s=18,450 parity_failures=2 (investigating)
Sam: Short update: two parity failures look like nondeterministic decimal rounding in float->quant conversion. saving diffs to replay_results/parity_diffs/
Rachel: Those rounding diffs are expected in some quant paths. we'll add tolerant comparison for numeric fields and full-token-string equality for final outputs.
Maria: I'll pull kernels for those request IDs and run micro-profiling. suspect mixed-dtype path.
Alex: Thanks team. Keep notes on lessons learned for the runbook. We'll reconvene if parity_failures > 0 after tolerant checks. :thumbsup:
